articles.headline: Roger Goodell says NFL targeting Tokyo game in 2027 or 2028
articles.description: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell reiterated his goal to hold a regular-season game in Tokyo and said he thinks it could happen in 2027 or 2028.
articles.body:
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell reiterated his goal to hold a regular-season game in Tokyo and said he thinks it could happen in 2027 or 2028.

"Listen, Tokyo is clearly on our list, whether it's next year or the year after," Goodell told "NFL Daily" on Friday. "It's coming at some point in the near future."

The comment sets a possible timeline for the NFL to play in a city that Goodell has previously targeted. He said in July at Fanatics Fest that he hoped to bring a regular-season game to Tokyo.

Goodell said the success and lessons learned from the San Francisco 49ers-Los Angeles Rams game in Melbourne, Australia, in Week 1 could help make a game in Japan happen.

"On a Friday morning at 10:30, to have 100,000 people in the stadium, it was just an incredible feeling for us. I think it's opened up new opportunities for us," Goodell told "NFL Daily." "The travel is something we think we can manage and do it without impacting negatively on the teams. So each of these we learned something from and we benefit and we also open those other doors."

The collective bargaining agreement allows the NFL to hold up to 10 international games per season. The league is playing nine this year -- including Sunday's first-ever regular-season game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints -- and executive vice president of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly said earlier this week that the bump up to 10 was under consideration for 2027.

O'Reilly also said playing in Asia was among the "new regions" being looked at.

The NFL has played 14 preseason games in Japan since 1976, most recently in 2005 between the Atlanta Falcons and Indianapolis Colts.

articles.headline: PSG-Lyon match moved to Monday amid Paris protests, NFL game
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain's clash with Lyon in Ligue 1 has been moved from Sunday to Monday evening at the request of Paris police.
articles.body:
PARIS -- Paris Saint-Germain's clash with Lyon in Ligue 1 has been moved from Sunday to Monday evening at the request of Paris police, the French league said on Friday.

The game was scheduled for 8:45 p.m. on Sunday -- only hours after France's first NFL game was taking place just north of Paris -- and will now be played at Parc des Princes in western Paris at 8:30 p.m. local time. Police resources are stretched in the French capital with mass protests planned for this weekend.

The LFP said in a statement that it "acknowledges the order issued by the police prefecture prohibiting the staging of the match between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais [on Sunday]."

The new time for PSG-Lyon clashes with the Ballon d'Or ceremony set for London. PSG players Ousmane Dembélé, Achraf Hakimi, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, João Neves, Willian Pacho, Fabián Ruiz, Ferran Torres and Vitinha are all nominated.

France's worst rioting in years saw city halls, other public buildings and thousands of businesses across the country impacted last weekend. There were scenes of widespread violence as police and protesters clashed, with shops destroyed and burned out, and local residents and shopkeepers left feeling exasperated by the chaos.

Last Saturday, 110 marches drew about 550,000 people across the country as they protested against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools.

Defending champion PSG and Lyon were level on 14 points at the top of Ligue 1 heading into this weekend's eighth round of games.

The NFL holds its first American football game in Paris on Sunday afternoon, when the Pittsburgh Steelers face the New Orleans Saints in their sold-out contest.

Around 80,000 fans are expected to attend the gridiron contest at Stade de France, which is just on the outskirts of Paris.

It can be reached via a short train ride from stations in Paris at Gare de Lyon, Gare du Nord and Châtelet or by subway lines.

articles.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin wins appeal, suspension for spitting reduced to fine
articles.description: Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr., has won his appeal to overturn the one-game suspension for supposedly spitting at an opponent in the win over the Raiders.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Buffalo Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr., has won his appeal to overturn the one-game suspension the NFL tagged him with for supposedly spitting at an opponent in the Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Franklin's suspension has been reduced to a fine of $14,926 per an NFL announcement.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that it would suspend Franklin without pay for one game because of a spitting incident said to have occurred on a fourth quarter extra point try. Franklin denied the allegation and moved quickly to appeal, saying in a social media post that he'll always do what it takes to defend himself but that he'd never spit at an opponent.

The suspension came in the wake of a second Bills defender, safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, being suspended for a high-profile spitting incident in the same game. Gardner-Johnson was disqualified from the game just before halftime after a referee witnessed Gardner-Johnson spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.

Unlike Gardner-Johnson, Franklin was not penalized or ejected in-game and no replays of the extra point in question available to the public can clearly show Franklin spitting.

Franklin's in his second year with the Bills and his seventh NFL season. He's logged six tackles in 2026, all on special teams. This included three tackles against the Raiders, matching his best mark since signing with the Bills.

Gardner-Johnson's suspension was upheld upon appeal.

The Bills are on bye this week. They'll return to action for a Week 8 game against Baltimore on Nov. 1 (1 p.m. ET, CBS). Gardner-Johnson will be eligible to return on Nov. 9 for "Monday Night Football" against the Minnesota Vikings (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN).

articles.headline: Knicks coaches waiting on rings; staffers hit by phishing offer, per report
articles.description: Knicks assistant coaches did not receive their championship rings during Tuesday's title ceremony, while a number of team employees instead were targeted by a phishing scam and will not receive rings at all, according to a report.
articles.body:
New York Knicks assistant coaches did not receive their championship rings during Tuesday's title ceremony ahead of the season opener, while a number of team employees instead were targeted by a Madison Square Garden phishing scam and will not receive rings at all, according to a report.

The Athletic reported Thursday that the assistant coaches were handed empty boxes during Tuesday's ceremony, in part because they had not yet been fitted for the rings.

The coaches' reaction to the delayed rings ranged from annoyance to anger, according to The Athletic.

But for some team employees in Knicks business operations and at Madison Square Garden, no rings are coming. Instead, they reportedly received an email last month saying "your Employee Championship Ring is here" that claimed that they could choose from a pair of options at "no cost to you."

When the employees clicked on a link in the email, The Athletic reported, they were informed that they had failed a phishing test and would have to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class.

"We are not disclosing anything about the rings," an MSG Sports spokesperson said in a statement to The Athletic.

The delay in some rings being handed out also occurred for the Oklahoma City Thunder after their 2025 title, The Athletic noted.

The Knicks ended a 53-year championship drought when they defeated the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals. On Tuesday, the team had not one but two new banners in the rafters, as one was also added to honor the Knicks' win in the NBA Cup during the 2025-26 season.

articles.headline: Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin out Sunday with shin injury
articles.description: Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday's game against the Lions with a shin injury.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- First Edgerrin Cooper, now Zaire Franklin. The Green Bay Packers have lost another inside linebacker due to injury, although at least the latest one is not season ending.

Franklin won't play on Sunday against the Detroit Lions because of a shin injury he sustained in practice on Thursday.

"Unfortunately there was a little collision," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Friday. "He got kneed in the shin, so he's gonna be out this game."

LaFleur said Franklin is not expected to go on injured reserve, meaning he will miss fewer than four games. Although it's his first year with the Packers after coming to Green Bay in an offseason trade with the Colts, the ninth-year veteran quickly became a key part of the defense. He was elected defensive captain, rare for someone in the first year with a team, and has been the signal caller for the defense.

Franklin ranked second on the team in tackles (41) and has two quarterback hits, a forced fumble and a pass breakup.

The Packers lost Cooper three weeks ago to a torn Achilles, so the Packers will have to face Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs without both of their starting inside linebackers. Gibbs ranks second in the NFL in yards from scrimmage per game (149.4) and fourth in rushing yards per game (100.8).

The Packers used two players to replace Cooper: Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. McDuffie has started but Hooper has played almost as many snaps in the rotation the last two weeks. Now Hopper, who had an interception in Week 5 against the Bears, will get a chance to start, too.

"He's done a great job," LaFleur said of Hopper. "His progression has been pretty cool to watch, just how he's developed over the years, especially I think we kinda got a good sense early on in training camp that he's on his way, so this will be a great opportunity for him to get even more reps."

On the offensive side, running back Josh Jacobs is on track to make his season debut on Sunday. He missed the first six games while on the commissioner exempt list and practiced this week for the first time since training camp.

"Yeah, I believe so," LaFleur said when asked if Jacobs is on track to play against the Lions. "But again, we'll get through it and see how he's feeling and the confidence he has in himself, which I think is pretty strong. But those conversations will take place after [Friday's] practice."

articles.headline: Chelsea's Xabi Alonso: Thibaut Courtois sees himself in Mike Penders
articles.description: Xabi Alonso believes understudy goalkeeper Mike Penders is ready for an extended spell in Chelsea's team after consulting on the 21-year-old with Thibaut Courtois.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso believes understudy goalkeeper Mike Penders is ready for an extended spell in Chelsea's team after consulting on the 21-year-old with Thibaut Courtois.

Penders became the club's youngest Premier League keeper when he replaced the injured Emiliano Martínez during the second half of last weekend's 2-0 win away at Everton, and will make his full league debut at home to Tottenham on Saturday.

Martínez, who joined from Aston Villa for £7 million ($9m) in August, has had surgery on a fractured jaw and is set to miss several weeks.

It means an earlier than expected opening in the team for Penders. He is considered internally to be the long-term No. 1 at Stamford Bridge and impressed in his first two starts for the club this season, Carabao Cup wins over Luton and Leeds.

Alonso was asked about similarities between the Belgium Under-21 international and his compatriot Courtois, with whom the Chelsea manager worked last season at Real Madrid.

"[There are] a lot, not just for the nationality," he said. "For the stature, both left-footed, both dominant in the air. I spoke with Thibaut when he was at the World Cup, I asked him about Mike. He said himself he could see resemblance.

"We need to help him, support him. He's a keeper for the present and for the future."

The two goalkeepers have followed a similar path. Both came through the ranks at Belgian side Genk before moving to Stamford Bridge while still relatively unknown outside their home country.

Courtois established himself in senior football during three years on loan at Atlético Madrid between 2011 and 2014, winning the LaLiga title and reaching the Champions League final before returning to west London to replace Petr Cech in Chelsea's goal.

Penders was loaned to Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, Chelsea's sister club, last season where he made 50 appearances in all competitions.

"He's ready," said Alonso. "He's been training well, he's played a couple of cup games, he's shown he has a good level.

"When he came on against Everton, he showed his personality, his qualities. We are fully convinced that Mike can play very well."

Chelsea opted to bring in Martínez to replace the error-prone Robert Sánchez, who performed poorly in Alonso's first game in charge, a 3-2 win over Fulham.

It is expected that Penders will eventually succeed the 34-year-old as the team's No. 1.

"We wanted to have the best possible options," said Alonso. "We decided that we would go for Emi and I think we have a good balance.

"Mike is a keeper for now and for the future. Having the support, learning with such an experienced goalkeeper as Emi, it's having a great impact on Mike."

articles.headline: Ex-Laker Dalton Knecht joins Knicks on two-way contract
articles.description: Former Lakers first-round pick Dalton Knecht has agreed to a two-way deal with the Knicks, his agents told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
It didn't take long for Dalton Knecht to find a new NBA team. Just days after the Los Angeles Lakers waived their 2024 first-round pick, the New York Knicks agreed to sign the 6-foot-6 forward to a two-way deal, his agents at Excel Sports Management told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

Knecht, selected with the No. 17 pick in 2024 after a standout junior season at the University of Tennessee, will look for a fresh start with the defending champs and try to tap into the promise he showed as a rookie in L.A.

During a nine-game stretch in November during the 2024-25 season, Knecht averaged 18.9 points on 55.4% shooting (52.2% from 3), 4.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists.

Knecht finished his rookie season averaging 9.1 points on 46.1% shooting (37.6% from 3) and 2.8 rebounds in 19.2 minutes across 78 games. In his second year, his playing time was cut to 10.2 minutes in 54 games, and he averaged 4.2 points on 45.5% shooting (34.2% from 3) and 1.4 rebounds.

The 25-year-old Knecht also received interest from the Cleveland Cavaliers, Sacramento Kings and Minnesota Timberwolves, sources told Charania.

New York will have to waive a two-way player to make room for Knecht. The Knicks currently have guard Jaden Akins and forwards Kevin McCullar Jr. and Tyler Nickel occupying their three allotted two-way roster spots.

articles.headline: Jets WR Adonai Mitchell to play, RB Breece Hall questionable vs. Dolphins
articles.description: Jets WR Adonai Mitchell, sidelined four games with a finger injury that required a surgical procedure, practiced all week and will play against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets' struggling offense will get one or possibly two key players back in the lineup Sunday.

Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, sidelined four games with a right-hand finger injury that required a surgical procedure, practiced all week and will play against the Miami Dolphins (0-5), coach Aaron Glenn said Friday.

The Jets are hopeful that running back Breece Hall also will return after missing three games with a quadriceps injury, but there's less certainty in his case. Hall, who practiced the past two days on a limited basis, is questionable for the game. Glenn said they will make the decision Sunday.

They could use a spark. The Jets (2-4) are averaging only 18.7 points per game (27th), with only four touchdowns in the past three games.

With Mitchell back, the Jets will have their top three receivers for the first time since Week 1. Mitchell, Garrett Wilson and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. have been on the field together for only four snaps -- the first series of the season opener. Cooper missed the next four games with an ankle injury, returning last week with a six-catch, 103-yard performance.

"Anytime we get the band back together, when they're all there and they get a chance to continue to build this relationship on the field, it's always critical," Glenn said, alluding to Mitchell's return.

Mitchell made nine receptions for 123 yards in the first two games. Before Week 3, he sustained a significant finger injury in practice when he caught it in a teammate's jersey, Glenn said. He practiced the next day. The Jets didn't think he'd be sidelined that long, so they didn't put him on injured reserve. About 10 days later, Mitchell underwent a procedure.

"With all the playmakers that we have, when you have a guy like AD out there, he can stretch the field, he can be a possession guy, and I think him, Garrett, Coop, they just present a lot of different challenges for the defense," quarterback Geno Smith said. "And so the more guys, the merrier."

Braelon Allen has filled in nicely for Hall, rushing for 253 yards over the last three games. Hall remains the starter, according to Glenn, adding that Allen will continue to get carries.

Left guard Dylan Parham, out three games with a knee injury, also could return Sunday. He returned to practice this week and is listed as questionable. The Jets could have their entire starting lineup intact for the first time since Week 1.

Glenn declined to comment on a report, confirmed by ESPN, that he was fined $250,000 by the league for his conduct toward game officials.

"I will keep that between me, the NFL and the refs," Glenn said.

articles.headline: Arsenal's Mikel Arteta admits Bukayo Saka injury signs are 'not good'
articles.description: Mikel Arteta did not deny Bukayo Saka's injury could be significant after the winger's struggles appeared to indicate "not good signs" for his prognosis.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta did not deny Bukayo Saka's injury could be significant after the winger's struggles appeared to indicate "not good signs" for his prognosis.

Saka, who sustained a quad injury during Arsenal's 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich, will undergo an MRI on Friday afternoon.

The Arsenal boss nevertheless urged "patience" while the medical team determines the nature and seriousness of the 25-year-old's issue.

"He's got quite a lot of fluid in the area, so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury, but we will probably know more tomorrow," said Arteta, explaining the decision to send Saka for the MRI.

"We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, his movement is restricted, they are not good signs.

"So, again, let's be a little bit patient so we can get a definitive assessment, and I will let you know."

Arteta insisted that he is not concerned about Saka's longevity, even with his injury history, saying: "I don't have that feeling at all, but certainly we have to be mindful of creating the right ecosystem around the player to fulfil all his qualities.

"We really need to understand now, when he comes back, whenever that is, how are we going to manage that load again? What is capable today to sustain having an impact in the team?"

Saka's absence for Saturday's clash with Everton could open the door for Max Dowman, who, in March, became the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer at 16 years and 73 days when he scored against the Toffees in the Gunners' 2-0 victory at the Emirates.

The last-gasp strike earned Dowman the club's goal of the season award, but he has made just three appearances for Arsenal this term.

Arteta agreed there was no doubt the situation would likely inspire some reflection.

"It would be a great story, if we win the game especially."
